claim: Intraocular fluid screening of 234 AMD patients identified high levels of IL-4.
source: Intraocular fluid screening of 234 AMD patients identified high levels of IL-4.
evidence: The manuscript states this finding directly in the abstract, and it is supported by data presented in Tables 1 and 2.

claim: The IL-4/IL-4 receptors (IL4Rs) controlled tube formation and global proangiogenic responses of bone marrow cells.
source: Our results indicate that the IL-4/IL-4 receptors (IL4Rs) controlled tube formation and global proangiogenic responses of bone marrow cells.
evidence: This claim is supported by tube formation assays (Figure 4) and transcriptional profiling data (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).

claim: CCR2+ bone marrow cells were recruited to form very early CNV lesions.
source: CCR2+ bone marrow cells were recruited to form very early CNV lesions.
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemical data showing CCR2+ cells in early CNV lesions (Figure 1, Figure 2—figure supplement 1).

claim: IL-4 rapidly induces CCL2, which enhances recruitment of CCR2+ bone marrow cells.
source: IL-4 rapidly induces CCL2, which enhances recruitment of CCR2+ bone marrow cells.
evidence: This is supported by RT-PCR data showing IL-4-induced CCL2 expression in EPCs (Figure 3a) and immunohistochemistry showing CCL2 expression (Figure 1c).

claim: IL-4 in bone marrow cells are critically required for CNV development.
source: For CNV development, IL-4 in bone marrow cells are critically required, and IL-4 directly promotes CNV formation mainly by IL-4R.
evidence: This is demonstrated by bone marrow chimera experiments showing that IL-4-deficient bone marrow impairs CNV formation (Figure 5).

claim: The IL-4/IL-4Rα axis contributes to pathological angiogenesis through communications with bone marrow cells leading to retinal degeneration.
source: The IL-4/IL-4Rα axis contributes to pathological angiogenesis through communications with bone marrow cells leading to retinal degeneration.
evidence: This is supported by experiments with IL-4Rα-deficient mice showing impaired CNV formation (Figure 2d) and bone marrow chimera studies (Figure 5).

claim: AMD patients had significantly higher levels of IL-4 in their aqueous humor than normal subjects.
source: The results showed that the AMD patients had significantly higher levels of IL-4 in their aqueous than in normal subjects (Table 1, Table 2).
evidence: This is directly supported by ELISA measurements presented in Table 1 showing IL-4 levels of 0.9 ± 0.1 pg/ml in AMD patients vs 0.3 ± 0.1 pg/ml in controls (p=0.0000).

claim: There was no significant elevation of IL-13 in AMD patients compared to controls.
source: In contrast, there was no significant elevation of IL-13.
evidence: This is supported by data in Table 1 showing IL-13 levels of 5.2 ± 0.7 pg/ml in AMD vs 3.8 ± 0.7 pg/ml in controls (NS).

claim: The level of IL-4 was significantly higher in typical AMD with a relative-risk ratio of 2.1.
source: The degree of elevation of IL-4 (quintile) had the highest relative-risk ratio of 2.5 for RAP (p=0.001, logistic regression analysis after age adjustments), followed by 2.1 for typical AMD (p=0.000) and 1.7 for PCV (p=0.000) (Table 2).
evidence: This is supported by multinomial logistic regression analysis data presented in Table 2.

claim: The level of IL-4 was significantly higher in polypoidal choroidal vasculopathy (PCV) with a relative-risk ratio of 1.7.
source: The degree of elevation of IL-4 (quintile) had the highest relative-risk ratio of 2.5 for RAP (p=0.001, logistic regression analysis after age adjustments), followed by 2.1 for typical AMD (p=0.000) and 1.7 for PCV (p=0.000) (Table 2).
evidence: This is supported by multinomial logistic regression analysis data presented in Table 2.

claim: The level of IL-4 was significantly higher in retinal angiomatous proliferation (RAP) with a relative-risk ratio of 2.5.
source: The degree of elevation of IL-4 (quintile) had the highest relative-risk ratio of 2.5 for RAP (p=0.001, logistic regression analysis after age adjustments), followed by 2.1 for typical AMD (p=0.000) and 1.7 for PCV (p=0.000) (Table 2).
evidence: This is supported by multinomial logistic regression analysis data presented in Table 2.

claim: The mRNA of IL-4 was elevated and peaked at 3 days after laser exposure in the murine CNV model.
source: Our results showed that the mRNA of IL-4 was elevated and peaked at 3 days after the laser exposure and then decreased (Figure 1a).
evidence: This is supported by RT-PCR data shown in Figure 1a.

claim: The mRNA of IL-4Rα had similar induction kinetics to IL-4, peaking at 3 days after laser exposure.
source: The mRNA of IL-4Rα also had similar induction kinetics.
evidence: This is supported by RT-PCR data shown in Figure 1a.

claim: The mRNA of CCR2 was elevated and peaked at 1 day after laser exposure, preceding IL-4 induction.
source: The mRNA of CCR2, a myeloid cell recruitment marker, was elevated, and the elevation preceded the mRNA of IL-4 induction by peaking at 1 day.
evidence: This is supported by RT-PCR data shown in Figure 1a.

claim: The mRNA of CD11b gradually increased after laser exposure.
source: The mRNA of CD11b gradually increased after the exposure.
evidence: This is supported by RT-PCR data shown in Figure 1a.

claim: IL-4 expressing cells accumulated along the margin of laser treated area at 3 days and then moved inwards.
source: Three day after the laser exposure, the IL-4-expressing cells were observed along the margins of the lesions and were present more centrally on day 7 (Figure 1b).
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemical data shown in Figure 1b.

claim: IL-4-expressing cells were largely CD11b+ and were considered to be myeloid- or macrophage-lineage cells.
source: The IL-4-expressing cells were largely CD11b+, and they were considered to be myeloid- or macrophage-lineage cells.
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemical co-localization data shown in Figure 1b.

claim: CCL2 was mainly associated with iba1-positive retinal microglial cells.
source: Our results showed that the CCL2 was mainly associated with iba1-positive retinal microglial cells (Figure 1c).
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemical co-localization data shown in Figure 1c.

claim: Systemic administration of IL-4 significantly exacerbated CNV formation in a dose dependent manner.
source: The IL-4 significantly exacerbated the CNV formation in a dose dependent way (Figure 2a).
evidence: This is supported by CNV size measurements in mice injected with different doses of IL-4 shown in Figure 2a.

claim: Systemic administration of IL-13 in the inductive phase had no significant effect on CNV formation.
source: Our results showed that a systemic administration of IL-13 in the inductive phase had no significant effect on CNV formation.
evidence: This is supported by CNV size measurements shown in Figure 2a.

claim: An IL-4 blockade by antibody injection significantly reduced the size of CNV.
source: Consistent with the effects of IL-4 administration, an IL-4 blockade significantly reduced the size of the CNV.
evidence: This is supported by CNV size measurements in mice injected with anti-IL-4 antibody shown in Figure 2b.

claim: A block of IL-13 by antibody injection had no significant effect on CNV formation.
source: In contrast, a block of IL-13 by an antibody injection had no significant effect on the CNV formation.
evidence: This is supported by CNV size measurements shown in Figure 2b.

claim: Il4-deficient mice were significantly impaired in CNV formation.
source: Consistent with the outcomes of the anti-IL-4 antibody exposure, Il4-deficient mice were significantly impaired in CNV formation which supports our finding that IL-4 is involved in the inductive phase of CNV.
evidence: This is supported by CNV size measurements in Il4-/- mice shown in Figure 2c.

claim: Il4ra-deficiency impaired CNV formation significantly.
source: Il4ra-deficiency impaired the CNV formation significantly (Figure 2d).
evidence: This is supported by CNV size measurements in Il4ra-/- mice shown in Figure 2d.

claim: IL-13Rα1-deficient mice showed no significant impairment in CNV formation.
source: When IL-13Rα1-deficient mice were tested for CNV formation, no significant impairment was observed.
evidence: This is supported by CNV size measurements in Il13ra1-/- mice shown in Figure 2d.

claim: Bone marrow-derived cells were incorporated into structures formed by CD31+ endothelial cells seven days after irradiation.
source: Seven days after irradiation, bone marrow-derived cells were incorporated into structures formed by CD31+ endothelial cells (Figure 2—video 1).
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemical data from bone marrow chimeric mice.

claim: Two weeks after laser exposure, bone marrow-derived cells were localized to isolectin-positive vascular endothelial cells in CNV lesions.
source: Two weeks after laser exposure, CNVs were formed as clusters of isolectin-positive vascular endothelial cells (red; Figure 2e). In the CNV lesion, bone marrow-derived cells (green) were localized to isolectin-positive vascular endothelial cells and CD31+ endothelial cells.
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemical data shown in Figure 2e.

claim: IL-4-positive cells were distributed at the margins of CNVs and precisely matched the bone marrow-derived cells.
source: IL-4-positive cells (yellow) were distributed at the margins of the CNVs and precisely matched the bone marrow-derived cells (green).
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemical co-localization data shown in Figure 2e.

claim: IL-4Rα-positive cells in the CNV partly overlapped the bone marrow-derived cells.
source: The IL-4Rα-positive cells (cyan) in the CNV, partly overlapped the bone marrow-derived cells.
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemical co-localization data shown in Figure 2e.

claim: IL-4 exposure significantly induced Ccl2 mRNA in bone marrow-derived EPCs in a dose dependent manner.
source: Of these, Ccl2 and Flt1 were significantly induced in a dose dependent manner after IL-4 exposure.
evidence: This is supported by RT-PCR data shown in Figure 3a.

claim: IL-4 exposure significantly induced Flt1 mRNA in bone marrow-derived EPCs in a dose dependent manner.
source: Of these, Ccl2 and Flt1 were significantly induced in a dose dependent manner after IL-4 exposure.
evidence: This is supported by RT-PCR data shown in Figure 3a.

claim: Anti-IL-4Rα antibody abolished IL-4-induced Ccl2 and Flt1 expression in EPCs.
source: When IL-4Rα was inhibited by an anti-IL-4Rα antibody, IL-4 failed to stimulate the EPCs from inducing the expression of Ccl2 and Flt1 (Figure 3a).
evidence: This is supported by RT-PCR data shown in Figure 3a.

claim: IL-4 stimulated retinal microvascular cells to induce Ccl2 and Flt1 in a dose dependent manner.
source: When retinal microvascular cells were tested for their effect on IL-4 by real-time reverse transcription PCR (RT-PCR), IL-4 was found to stimulate the induction of Ccl2/Flt1 (Figure 3b).
evidence: This is supported by RT-PCR data shown in Figure 3b.

claim: IL-4 exposure significantly stimulated CCL2 protein secretion from EPCs after 24 hours.
source: IL-4-exposed EPCs had a significant increase in the secretion of CCL2 (p=0.000) and VEGFR-1 (p=0.000) after 24 hr exposure to IL-4 (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by ELISA data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: IL-4 exposure significantly stimulated VEGFR-1 protein secretion from EPCs after 24 hours.
source: IL-4-exposed EPCs had a significant increase in the secretion of CCL2 (p=0.000) and VEGFR-1 (p=0.000) after 24 hr exposure to IL-4 (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by ELISA data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: EPCs from Il4ra-deficient mice did not induce Ccl2 and Flt1 in response to IL-4 or IL-13.
source: EPCs from Il4ra-deficient mice did not induce Ccl2 and Flt1 in response to IL-4 or IL-13 (Figure 3c).
evidence: This is supported by RT-PCR data shown in Figure 3c.

claim: When Il13ra1-deficient EPCs were stimulated by IL-4, Ccl2 and Flt1 were still induced.
source: When Il13ra1-deficient EPC mice were stimulated by IL-4, Ccl2 and Flt1 were still induced (Figure 3d) indicating that IL-13Rα1 was not necessary for IL-4 stimulation.
evidence: This is supported by RT-PCR data shown in Figure 3d.

claim: When Il13ra1-deficient EPCs were stimulated with IL-13, Ccl2 and Flt1 were not induced.
source: When Il13ra1-deficient EPC mice were stimulated with IL-13, Ccl2 and Flt1 were not induced.
evidence: This is supported by RT-PCR data shown in Figure 3d.

claim: EPCs of Il4-deficient mice still induced IL-4 and IL-13-mediated Ccl2 and Flt1 induction.
source: The results indicated that the EPCs of Il4-deificient mice still induced IL-4 and the IL-13-mediated Ccl2 and Flt1 induction (Figure 3e).
evidence: This is supported by RT-PCR data shown in Figure 3e.

claim: Murine IL-4 exposure significantly stimulated tube formation of murine retinal microvascular endothelial cells in vitro.
source: When murine retinal microvascular endothelial cells were tested for tube formation by IL-4 or VEGF, both stimulated significant tube formation (Figure 4a).
evidence: This is supported by tube formation assay data shown in Figure 4a.

claim: Anti-IL-4 and IL-4Rα antibodies abolished IL-4-induced tube formation in retinal vascular endothelial cells.
source: Anti-IL-4 and IL-4Rα antibodies abolished the IL-4-induced tube formation.
evidence: This is supported by tube formation assay data shown in Figure 4a.

claim: Human IL-4 exposure significantly stimulated tube formation of human retinal microvascular endothelial cells in vitro.
source: IL-4 exposure stimulated tube formation by human retinal vascular endothelial cells, and anti-IL-4 and IL-4Rα antibodies blocked this effect.
evidence: This is supported by tube formation assay data shown in Figure 4a.

claim: IL-4 significantly stimulated tube formation by EPCs derived from wild type bone marrow cells.
source: For the wild type bone marrow cells, IL-4 significantly stimulated tube formation by the EPCs (Figure 4bc).
evidence: This is supported by tube formation assay data shown in Figure 4b and 4c.

claim: IL-4-induced tube formation was blocked when bone marrow cells were deficient in Il4ra.
source: This IL-4-induced tube formation was blocked when the bone marrow cells were deficient of Il4ra.
evidence: This is supported by tube formation assay data shown in Figure 4b and 4c.

claim: Inhibition of VEGF receptor tyrosine kinase or VEGF receptor 2 did not significantly inhibit IL-4-induced tube formation.
source: However, the inhibition of the VEGF receptor tyrosine kinase or VEGF receptor 2 did not significantly inhibit tube formation (Figure 4b).
evidence: This is supported by tube formation assay data with VEGF receptor inhibitors shown in Figure 4b.

claim: IL-4-induced tube formation was blocked when bone marrow cells were deficient in Il4.
source: The IL-4-induced tube formation was blocked when the cells were deficient of Il4 but not by Il13ra1 deficiency (Figure 4c).
evidence: This is supported by tube formation assay data shown in Figure 4c.

claim: IL-13 stimulated tube formation by bone marrow-derived EPCs.
source: IL-13 also stimulated tube formation by bone marrow-derived EPCs.
evidence: This is supported by tube formation assay data shown in Figure 4c.

claim: IL-13-induced tube formation was abolished when bone marrow cells were deficient in Il4 and Il13ra1.
source: This response was abolished when the bone marrow cells were deficient in Il4 and Il13ra1.
evidence: This is supported by tube formation assay data shown in Figure 4c.

claim: IL-4-stimulated EPCs showed significant association with homing of cells (Z score = 2.798, p=8.3 × 10−5).
source: Analysis of the functions of IL-4-stimulated EPCs indicated significant association with the homing of the cells (Z score = 2.798, p=8.3 × 10−5), angiogenesis (Z score = 2.781, p=1.8 × 10−4), activation of macrophages (Z score = 2.731, p=1.0 × 10−5), and recruitment of myeloid cells (Z score = 2.606, p=2.8 × 10−10) (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by Ingenuity Pathway Analysis of microarray data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: IL-4-stimulated EPCs showed significant association with angiogenesis (Z score = 2.781, p=1.8 × 10−4).
source: Analysis of the functions of IL-4-stimulated EPCs indicated significant association with the homing of the cells (Z score = 2.798, p=8.3 × 10−5), angiogenesis (Z score = 2.781, p=1.8 × 10−4), activation of macrophages (Z score = 2.731, p=1.0 × 10−5), and recruitment of myeloid cells (Z score = 2.606, p=2.8 × 10−10) (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by Ingenuity Pathway Analysis of microarray data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: IL-4-stimulated EPCs showed significant association with activation of macrophages (Z score = 2.731, p=1.0 × 10−5).
source: Analysis of the functions of IL-4-stimulated EPCs indicated significant association with the homing of the cells (Z score = 2.798, p=8.3 × 10−5), angiogenesis (Z score = 2.781, p=1.8 × 10−4), activation of macrophages (Z score = 2.731, p=1.0 × 10−5), and recruitment of myeloid cells (Z score = 2.606, p=2.8 × 10−10) (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by Ingenuity Pathway Analysis of microarray data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: IL-4-stimulated EPCs showed significant association with recruitment of myeloid cells (Z score = 2.606, p=2.8 × 10−10).
source: Analysis of the functions of IL-4-stimulated EPCs indicated significant association with the homing of the cells (Z score = 2.798, p=8.3 × 10−5), angiogenesis (Z score = 2.781, p=1.8 × 10−4), activation of macrophages (Z score = 2.731, p=1.0 × 10−5), and recruitment of myeloid cells (Z score = 2.606, p=2.8 × 10−10) (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by Ingenuity Pathway Analysis of microarray data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Il4-deficient mice with Il4-/- bone marrow developed the smallest size CNVs of all the chimeric mice.
source: The Il4-deficient mice with Il4-/- bone marrow developed the smallest size CNVs of all the chimeric mice.
evidence: This is supported by CNV size measurements in bone marrow chimeric mice shown in Figure 5a.

claim: Impaired CNV formation in Il4-deficient mice was completely restored by transplantation of bone marrow cells from wild type mice.
source: This impaired CNV formation was completely restored by the transplantation of bone marrow cells from wild type mice.
evidence: This is supported by CNV size measurements in bone marrow chimeric mice shown in Figure 5a.

claim: Wild type mice with Il4-/- bone marrow were still impaired for CNV formation.
source: In contrast, wild type mice with Il4-/- bone marrow were still impaired for CNV formation which indicated that the host resident cell-derived IL-4 is limited in this activity (Figure 5a).
evidence: This is supported by CNV size measurements in bone marrow chimeric mice shown in Figure 5a.

claim: Il4ra-deficient mice with Il4ra-/- bone marrow cells were impaired in the formation of CNVs.
source: Consistent with the results shown in Figure 2, Il4ra-deficient mice with Il4ra-/- bone marrow cells were impaired in the formation of CNVs.
evidence: This is supported by CNV size measurements in bone marrow chimeric mice shown in Figure 5a.

claim: Impairment of CNV formation in Il4ra-deficient mice was restored by transplantation of wild type bone marrow cells.
source: This impairment was restored by the transplantation of wild type bone marrow cells (Figure 5a).
evidence: This is supported by CNV size measurements in bone marrow chimeric mice shown in Figure 5a.

claim: IL-4-positive cells in CNV lesions precisely matched bone marrow-derived cells in Il4-deficient mice reconstituted with wild type bone marrow.
source: The IL-4-positive cells precisely matched the bone marrow-derived cells (green).
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemical co-localization data shown in Figure 5b.

claim: IL-4Rα positivity partly overlapped with bone marrow-derived cells in CNV lesions.
source: In contrast, the IL-4Rα positivity partly overlapped with that of the bone marrow-derived cells.
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemical co-localization data shown in Figure 5b.

claim: Bone marrow-derived cells are the major producer of IL-4 in CNV lesions.
source: This indicated that bone marrow-derived cells are the major producer of IL-4, and bone marrow-derived cells and resident cells in the CNV via IL-4Rα recognized their signals.
evidence: This is inferred from immunohistochemical data showing IL-4 expression co-localizing with bone marrow-derived cells in Figure 5b.

claim: The mean age of AMD patients was 74.1 ± 0.6 years.
source: The mean age of the patients with AMD was 74.1 ± 0.6 years, and it was 74.9 ± 1.0 years for the normal subjects.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section describing the patient cohort.

claim: The mean age of normal subjects was 74.9 ± 1.0 years.
source: The mean age of the patients with AMD was 74.1 ± 0.6 years, and it was 74.9 ± 1.0 years for the normal subjects.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section describing the patient cohort.

claim: Age-associated sterile inflammation can cause dysregulated choroidal neovascularization (CNV) as age-related macular degeneration (AMD).
source: Age-associated sterile inflammation can cause dysregulated choroidal neovascularization (CNV) as age-related macular degeneration (AMD).
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a general premise of the study.

claim: Choroidal neovascularizations (CNVs) develop in the subretinal space in AMD.
source: Choroidal (CNVs) develop in the subretinal space, and the CNVs lead to degeneration of the photoreceptor cells, infiltration by inflammatory cells, activation of microglia, and ganglion cell loss (Beck et al., 2016; Copland et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Beck et al., 2016 and Copland et al., 2018.

claim: CNVs lead to degeneration of photoreceptor cells, infiltration by inflammatory cells, activation of microglia, and ganglion cell loss.
source: Choroidal (CNVs) develop in the subretinal space, and the CNVs lead to degeneration of the photoreceptor cells, infiltration by inflammatory cells, activation of microglia, and ganglion cell loss (Beck et al., 2016; Copland et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Beck et al., 2016 and Copland et al., 2018.

claim: The pathology of AMD is coupled with senescence-associated para-inflammation characterized by secretion of IL-6, IL-8, CCL2, and CX3CL1.
source: The pathology of AMD is coupled with senescence-associated para-inflammation, which is characterized by the secretion of IL-6, IL-8, CCL2, and CX3CL1 (Sasaki et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Sasaki et al., 2010.

claim: CCL2 plays an important role in recruiting bone marrow cells, monocytes, and macrophages to ocular neovascularizations.
source: Of these, CCL2 plays an important role in recruiting bone marrow cells, monocytes, and macrophages to the ocular neovascularizations.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the Introduction.

claim: The bone marrow plays an important role by supplying new vascular endothelial cells and macrophages to the retina.
source: In this disease process, the bone marrow plays an important role by supplying new vascular endothelial cells and macrophages to the retina (Gao et al., 2016; Zhou et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Gao et al., 2016 and Zhou et al., 2017.

claim: M1 macrophages are functionally classified as pro-inflammatory.
source: The M1 macrophages are functionally classified as pro-inflammatory, and the M2 macrophages are classified as anti-inflammatory, and both types are recruited to damaged tissues.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the Introduction.

claim: M2 macrophages are functionally classified as anti-inflammatory.
source: The M1 macrophages are functionally classified as pro-inflammatory, and the M2 macrophages are classified as anti-inflammatory, and both types are recruited to damaged tissues.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the Introduction.

claim: M2 macrophages are induced by IL-4.
source: The M2 macrophages are induced by IL-4, and it has been suggested that they have disease-regulating functions as opposed to the M1 macrophages (Zhou et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Zhou et al., 2017.

claim: IL-4 has regulatory and neuroprotective functions in Alzheimer's disease.
source: The concept of IL-4 as a regulatory and neuroprotective cytokine is supported by the findings in other neurodegenerative diseases including Alzheimer's disease (Kiyota et al., 2010) and Parkinson's disease (Chitnis and Weiner, 2017; Zhao et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Kiyota et al., 2010.

claim: IL-4 has regulatory and neuroprotective functions in Parkinson's disease.
source: The concept of IL-4 as a regulatory and neuroprotective cytokine is supported by the findings in other neurodegenerative diseases including Alzheimer's disease (Kiyota et al., 2010) and Parkinson's disease (Chitnis and Weiner, 2017; Zhao et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Chitnis and Weiner, 2017 and Zhao et al., 2006.

claim: IL-4 is known to be a potent inhibitor of angiogenesis.
source: Moreover, IL-4 is known to be a potent inhibitor of angiogenesis (Haas et al., 2006; Volpert et al., 1998), and thus may prevent pathological angiogenesis in eyes with AMD.
evidence: This is supported by citations to Haas et al., 2006 and Volpert et al., 1998.

claim: IL-4 inhibits tumor growth by inhibiting angiogenesis.
source: IL-4 inhibits tumor growth by inhibiting angiogenesis (Volpert et al., 1998) and also blocks corneal neovascularization induced by basic fibroblast growth factor.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Volpert et al., 1998.

claim: IL-4 blocks corneal neovascularization induced by basic fibroblast growth factor.
source: IL-4 inhibits tumor growth by inhibiting angiogenesis (Volpert et al., 1998) and also blocks corneal neovascularization induced by basic fibroblast growth factor.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section.

claim: IL-4 significantly increases the survival of retinal ganglion cells in axotomized retinas.
source: In axotomized retinas, the retinal ganglion cells are severely damaged by nitric oxide synthesis by activated glial cells. IL-4 significantly increases the survival of retinal ganglion cells, and prevents neurodegeneration caused by glial cell activation (Koeberle et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Koeberle et al., 2004.

claim: IL-4 can completely block the death of photoreceptors in the thapsigargin-induced rod photoreceptor cell death model.
source: In the thapsigargin-induced rod photoreceptor cell death model, IL-4 can completely block the death of the photoreceptors (Adão-Novaes et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Adão-Novaes et al., 2009.

claim: During retinal differentiation, IL-4 modulates the proliferation of retinal cells and promotes photoreceptor differentiation.
source: During the differentiation of the retina, IL-4 modulates the proliferation of the retinal cells and promotes photoreceptor differentiation (da Silva et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citation to da Silva et al., 2008.

claim: Higher levels of M1 than M2 type mRNAs were observed in advanced stage AMD patients.
source: Higher levels of M1 than M2 type mRNAs were observed in advanced stage AMD patients (Cao et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Cao et al., 2011.

claim: M1 macrophages counteract M2 macrophages by secretion of interferon-γ.
source: The M1 macrophages counteract the M2 type by the secretion of interferon-γ.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the Discussion.

claim: M1 types of IFNAR1+ macrophages have been reported to be protective in laser-induced CNV.
source: However, the M1 types of IFNAR1+ macrophages have been reported to be protective in laser-induced CNV (Lückoff et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Lückoff et al., 2016.

claim: In the retina, vascular repair and neovascularization are performed largely by circulating EPCs because mature vascular endothelial cells for proliferation are limited.
source: In the retina, vascular repair and neovascularization are performed largely by circulating EPCs because mature vascular endothelial cells for proliferation are limited (Caballero et al., 2007; Grant et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Caballero et al., 2007 and Grant et al., 2002.

claim: EPCs are present in the bone marrow or are peripheral blood mononuclear cells.
source: EPCs are present in the bone marrow or are peripheral blood mononuclear cells (Rohde et al., 2006; Schatteman and Awad, 2003; Schmeisser et al., 2001), and they can differentiate into endothelial cells as late EPCs and be incorporated into the vasculature system.
evidence: This is supported by citations to Rohde et al., 2006, Schatteman and Awad, 2003, and Schmeisser et al., 2001.

claim: EPCs can differentiate into endothelial cells as late EPCs and be incorporated into the vasculature system.
source: EPCs are present in the bone marrow or are peripheral blood mononuclear cells (Rohde et al., 2006; Schatteman and Awad, 2003; Schmeisser et al., 2001), and they can differentiate into endothelial cells as late EPCs and be incorporated into the vasculature system.
evidence: This is supported by citations to Rohde et al., 2006, Schatteman and Awad, 2003, and Schmeisser et al., 2001.

claim: IL-4 induces proinflammatory phenotypes and causes vascular leakage or increased turnover of endothelial cells.
source: For example, IL-4 induces proinflammatory phenotypes and causes vascular leakage or increased turnover of endothelial cells (Kotowicz et al., 2004; Lee et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Kotowicz et al., 2004 and Lee et al., 2010.

claim: IL-4 stimulates human umbilical vascular endothelial cells (HUVEC) to induce proinflammatory cytokines including CCL2, VCAM-1, and IL-6.
source: IL-4 stimulates human umbilical vascular endothelial cells (HUVEC) cells to induce proinflammatory cytokines including CCL2, VCAM-1, and IL-6, as a signature of global transcriptional responses (Lee et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Lee et al., 2004.

claim: IL-4-induced proinflammatory responses appear to be a general characteristic of vascular endothelial cells including coronary arterial endothelial cells.
source: These responses appear to be a general characteristics of vascular endothelial cells including coronary arterial endothelial cells (Skaria et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Skaria et al., 2016.

claim: CD31 is highly expressed on endothelial cells and is commonly used as an endothelial cell marker.
source: To identify an endothelial lineage, we used CD31 or isolectin staining because CD31 is highly expressed on endothelial cells and is commonly used as an endothelial cell marker.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the Discussion.

claim: CD31 can also be expressed on other lineage cells including T cells, B cells, dendritic cells (DCs), neutrophils, monocytes, and macrophages.
source: However, CD31 can also be expressed on other lineage cells including T cells, B cells, dendritic cells (DCs; Clement et al., 2014), neutrophils, monocytes, and macrophage (Merchand-Reyes et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Clement et al., 2014 and Merchand-Reyes et al., 2019.

claim: Bone marrow cells play pivotal roles in CNV formation.
source: Importantly, bone marrow-derived cells do play pivotal roles in the CNV formation.
evidence: This is concluded from the bone marrow chimera experiments presented in the study.

claim: Damages of the retina and choroidal tissue release signals to the bone marrow to repair vascular damage.
source: In conclusion, damages of the retina and choroidal tissue release signals to the bone marrow to repair the vascular damage.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental findings in the study.

claim: Calling and/or fate determining signals for bone marrow-derived cells are governed by IL-4.
source: Calling and/or fate determining signals are governed by IL-4.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental findings showing IL-4's role in bone marrow cell recruitment and differentiation.

claim: IL-4 may serve as a therapeutic target to treat AMD.
source: IL-4 may serve as a therapeutic target to treat this visual disorder.
evidence: This is a speculative conclusion based on the findings of the study.

claim: Aqueous humor was collected from 234 patients with clinically-diagnosed AMD and impaired central vision.
source: To accomplish this, aqueous humor was collected from the eyes of 234 patients with clinically-diagnosed AMD and impaired central vision and 104 normal subjects undergoing routine cataract surgery.
evidence: This describes the patient cohort used in the study.

claim: Aqueous humor was collected from 104 normal subjects undergoing routine cataract surgery.
source: To accomplish this, aqueous humor was collected from the eyes of 234 patients with clinically-diagnosed AMD and impaired central vision and 104 normal subjects undergoing routine cataract surgery.
evidence: This describes the control cohort used in the study.

claim: Bone marrow cells were cultured for differentiation to late EPCs for 2 weeks.
source: To do this, bone marrow cells were cultured for differentiation to late EPCs for 2 weeks and exposed to IL-4.
evidence: This describes the experimental protocol used in the study.

claim: IL-4 exposure did not affect the induction of Vegf, Kdr, Flt4, Tek, Angpt1, Selp, Ednra, Cdh5, F2r, or F2rl1 mRNAs in EPCs after 24 hours.
source: IL-4 exposure did not affect the induction of angiogenesis-related mRNAs of EPCs including Vegf, Kdr, Flt4, Tek, Angpt1, Selp, Ednra, Cdh5, F2r, F2rl1 after 24 hr. (RT-PCR, n = 5–8/group).
evidence: This is supported by RT-PCR data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: VEGF did not significantly induce Ccl2 and Flt1 in EPCs.
source: However, VEGF did not significantly induce Ccl2 and Flt1.
evidence: This is supported by RT-PCR data shown in Figure 3c.

claim: IL-4Rα is the major receptor for IL-4 to induce the expression of CCL2 and VEGFR-1.
source: Collectively, these findings indicate that IL-4Rα is the major receptor for IL-4 to induce the expression of CCL2 and VEGFR-1, and the IL-13Rα1 can substitute for their induction mainly through IL-13.
evidence: This is concluded from experiments with Il4ra-deficient and Il13ra1-deficient EPCs shown in Figures 3c and 3d.

claim: IL-13Rα1 can substitute for IL-4Rα in inducing CCL2 and VEGFR-1 expression mainly through IL-13.
source: Collectively, these findings indicate that IL-4Rα is the major receptor for IL-4 to induce the expression of CCL2 and VEGFR-1, and the IL-13Rα1 can substitute for their induction mainly through IL-13.
evidence: This is concluded from experiments with Il4ra-deficient and Il13ra1-deficient EPCs shown in Figures 3c and 3d.

claim: Recruitment of GFP+ bone marrow-derived cells peaked at 3 days after irradiation.
source: Recruitment of GFP+ bone marrow-derived cells (green) peaked at 3 days after irradiation.
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemical data from bone marrow chimeric mice shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Bone marrow-derived cells in the inductive phase were CD11b+ lineage and positive for CCL2.
source: Bone marrow-derived cells in this phase were CD11b+ lineage, and they were positive for CCL2.
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemical data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Bone marrow-derived cells in the inductive phase did not express iba1 and were morphologically distinct from microglial cells.
source: These bone marrow cells did not express iba1 and were morphologically distinct from microglial cells.
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemical data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: The co-localization of marrow-derived cells with CD31+ endothelial cells indicated that bone marrow-derived cells may be able to differentiate into endothelial cells.
source: The co-localization of the marrow-derived cells with CD31+ endothelial cells indicated that the bone marrow-derived cells may be able to differentiate into endothelial cells.
evidence: This is inferred from immunohistochemical co-localization data shown in Figure 2e.

claim: Bone marrow cells will also differentiate into non-endothelial cell lineage and serve as providers of CNV-forming signals.
source: Alternatively, bone marrow cells will also differentiate into non-endothelial cell lineage and serve as providers of CNV-forming signals.
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental findings in the study.

claim: IL-4R+ bone marrow-derived cells are incorporated into CNV as late EPCs or non-endothelial lineage cells, together with resident cell-derived endothelial cells.
source: As a late phase phenomenon, the IL-4R+ bone marrow-derived cells are incorporated into the CNV presumably as late EPCs or non-endothelial lineage cells, together with the resident cell-derived endothelial cells.
evidence: This is inferred from immunohistochemical data and the temporal analysis of bone marrow cell recruitment.

claim: Bone marrow-derived cells contribute to both early and late phases of CNV formation using IL-4 as the fate determinant.
source: We propose that the bone marrow-derived cells contribute to both phases using IL-4 as the fate determinant.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental findings showing IL-4's role throughout CNV formation.

claim: Microglial cells migrated to the surface of the CNV.
source: The microglial cells migrated to surface of the CNV (Figure 1—video 1).
evidence: This is supported by video microscopy data referenced as Figure 1—video 1.

claim: IL-4 expressions followed by myeloid cell activation were early events acting at the inductive phase of CNV formation.
source: Thus, IL-4 expressions followed by myeloid cell activation were early events acting at the inductive phase of the CNV formation.
evidence: This is concluded from the temporal analysis of IL-4 and myeloid cell marker expression shown in Figure 1.

claim: Microglial cells were the initial stimulators in CNV formation.
source: This indicated that they were the initial stimulators.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that CCL2 was mainly associated with iba1-positive microglial cells at early time points.

claim: The kinetics of Iba1-, CCL2-, and CD11b-positive cells after laser exposure was consistent with that of the mRNA induction.
source: The kinetics of Iba1-, CCL2-, and CD11b-positive cells after laser exposure was consistent with that of the mRNA induction (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemical data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: The concept of cell level and organ level quorum sensing has been recently proposed to explain dysregulated repair processes after organ damage.
source: To explain the dysregulated repair process after organ damage, the concept of cell level and organ level quorum sensing has been recently proposed (Antonioli et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Antonioli et al., 2018.

claim: Hair follicle injury sensed by a macrophage-mediated circuit via CCL2 is a well-known example of quorum sensing at the organ level.
source: Hair follicle injury sensed by a macrophage-mediated circuit via CCL2 is a well-known example of quorum sensing at the organ level (Chen et al., 2015; Feng et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Chen et al., 2015 and Feng et al., 2017.

claim: The quorum sensing circuit mediated by microglia-derived CCL2 appears to operate in new vessel formation in the retina together with a late IL-4 modulator.
source: The quorum sensing circuit mediated by microglia-derived CCL2 also appears to operate in new vessel formation in the retina together with a late IL-4 modulator.
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental findings showing early CCL2 expression by microglia followed by IL-4 expression.

claim: CD11b was present in CNV lesions at 12 hours after laser exposure.
source: We observed the presence of CD11b in the CNV lesions at 12 hr which would indicate that monocyte/macrophage cells had arrived soon after the beginning of the CNV.
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemical data.

claim: Retinal pigment epithelial cells and microglial cells are the major sources of CCL2 cells in the retina.
source: CCL2 recruits circulating mononuclear cells from the bone marrow, and the retinal pigment epithelial cells and microglial cells are the major sources of the CCL2 cells in the retina (Feng et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Feng et al., 2017.

claim: The monocyte/macrophage recruiting signal, including CCL2, appears to be the first signal in the formation of CNVs.
source: Thus, the monocyte/macrophage recruiting signal, including CCL2, appears to be the first signal in the formation of CNVs.
evidence: This is concluded from the temporal analysis showing early CCL2 expression.

claim: CCL2 is involved in the formation of retinal neovascularization.
source: It was reported that CCL2 is involved in the formation of retinal neovascularization (Sennlaub et al., 2013; Yoshida et al., 2003).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Sennlaub et al., 2013 and Yoshida et al., 2003.

claim: CCL2/CCR2 signals recruit a heterogeneous collection of monocyte/macrophage lineage cells and presumably do not determine their fate.
source: However, the CCL2/CCR2 signals recruit a heterogeneous collection of monocyte/macrophage lineage cells and presumably do not determine their fate (Grochot-Przeczek et al., 2013; Pearson, 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Grochot-Przeczek et al., 2013 and Pearson, 2010.

claim: Bone marrow-derived cells and macrophages are critical contributors to retinal and choroidal neovascularization.
source: Bone marrow-derived cells and macrophages are critical contributors to retinal and choroidal neovascularization (Gao et al., 2016; Zhou et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Gao et al., 2016 and Zhou et al., 2017.
